title: Rashid Khan Blames Shot Selection as India Close In on T20I Clean Sweep
excerpt: After Afghanistan lost the second T20I by seven wickets in Delhi to hand India the series, Rashid Khan admitted his side misread the conditions and batted poorly, while BCCI vice-president Rajiv Shukla predicted a clean sweep in Thursday's final match at the Arun Jaitley Stadium.
body:
• India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets in the second T20I in New Delhi on Tuesday, taking an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.
  • Captain Rashid Khan admitted Afghanistan misread the conditions, failed to use the powerplay and made poor shot selections, calling Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium a venue that demands totals of 200-plus.
  • Chasing 160, India finished the job in 14.5 overs, led by Sanju Samson's 57, Abhishek Sharma's 39 and an unbeaten 38 from Ishan Kishan.
  • BCCI vice-president Rajiv Shukla predicted a clean sweep, saying India would also win the third and final T20I on Thursday, September 18, at the same venue.

NEW DELHI — Afghanistan captain Rashid Khan has taken blunt responsibility for his side's series defeat to India, admitting his batters misread the conditions, squandered the powerplay and threw away their wickets with poor shot selection in the second T20I on Tuesday.

India's seven-wicket victory at the Arun Jaitley Stadium — chasing 160 in just 14.5 overs — gave the Shreyas Iyer-led hosts an unassailable 2-0 lead with the final match still to come on Thursday. Speaking to IANS on Wednesday, Rashid said the 159/8 his side managed was nowhere near enough on a ground where big totals are the norm.

"We didn't read the conditions properly. We have played a lot in Delhi and you have to post 200-210-220 runs if you want to win the match. Our shot selection was not at that level. This is a good learning for us and next time, we will play with a better mind and better shot selection."

— Rashid Khan, Afghanistan captain

Rashid also turned the criticism inward. After a forgettable outing in the series opener, he came out with greater intent in the second game, striking 28 with the bat before claiming 3-36 with the ball.

"In the first match, I played ten balls and scored only one run. I was feeling very bad. Looking at the scoreboard, I said, 'This is not me. How can I score 1 run off 10 balls?' So I had the mind that the next time I go, I will show the intent, play positively."

— Rashid Khan

How India Dominated

The pattern across both games has been near-identical. In the first T20I, India chased 157 with seven wickets to spare; in the second, they overhauled 160 with the same margin. Afghanistan's batting offered only flashes of resistance: opener Rahmanullah Gurbaz registered a duck in both matches, and Ibrahim Zadran's 37 plus a 48-run sixth-wicket stand between Mohammad Nabi and Rashid Khan were the only passages of control.

Nitish Kumar Reddy and Arshdeep Singh shared five wickets to keep Afghanistan in check, and India's chases were calm throughout. In the second game, Sanju Samson top-scored with 57, Abhishek Sharma contributed 39 and Ishan Kishan remained unbeaten on 38 to seal the win.

The Clean-Sweep Call

BCCI vice-president and MP Rajiv Shukla expressed full confidence that India would finish the job on Thursday. "The series is going very well. We have already won the series, and we will win the third match as well," Shukla said on the sidelines of an event in New Delhi on Wednesday.

The final T20I, also at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, doubles as a tune-up ahead of the Asian Games. With the series decided, team management is expected to use the dead rubber to test fringe players and squad depth under match conditions.

The Friendship Off the Field

Between the games, the Afghanistan Cricket Board hosted the Indian squad for a dinner in New Delhi on Wednesday, where players from both sides swapped notes on their shared Indian Premier League experiences. Ishan Kishan spoke warmly of batting alongside Mohammad Nabi at Mumbai Indians, saying Nabi had guided him through batting sessions and planning against different bowlers. Abhishek Sharma added that facing Afghanistan's aggressive brand of cricket sharpens young Indian players — a nod to a fixture that has grown into one of the sport's friendlier rivalries.

What's Next

Thursday's decider is about two things: whether India complete the clean sweep Shukla is predicting, and whether Afghanistan can find the 200-plus formula Rashid says Delhi demands. For India, it is also a selection checkpoint before the Asian Games. For Afghanistan, it is a final chance to leave New Delhi with something other than lessons.
image_caption: Afghanistan players celebrate a wicket during the T20I series against India. Captain Rashid Khan took 3-36 in the second match in Delhi, where the visitors lost by seven wickets to hand India the series.
nri_angle: The series, hosted in India with Afghanistan playing in front of Indian crowds, is closely followed by Afghan diaspora fans in the US and Europe and by Indian diaspora audiences whose IPL ties to Afghan stars like Rashid Khan and Mohammad Nabi add a personal thread to the fixture.
